alex: Heads up — after the CUDA/driver bump on the inference fleet (CUDA 12.1 -> 12.3 driver) we're seeing a 20-35% regression in token throughput on p4d for many models. Oddly the impact is sequence-length dependent: tiny for seq<=128, large around seq≈512, and moderate for long seqs.
jamie: Oof. Do you have profiler traces or kernel timings? Which kernels regressed?
alex: Pasted the short perf snippet from the microbenchmark run on a canary node:```
Model: ggml-like transformer, batch=8
seq=128  mean token/s = 4200
seq=512  mean token/s = 1800  (prev: ~2700)
seq=2048 mean token/s = 900   (prev: ~1000)
CUDA kernels:
  matmul_16x64_tiled  time=42ms  (was 27ms)
  matmul_32x32_fast   time=18ms  (was 16ms)
  attn_reduce_kernel  time=9ms   (unchanged)
  kv_cache_copy       time=6ms   (unchanged)
nvprof snippet shows matmul_16x64_tiled is hot and much slower after driver bump.```
priya: That points to a kernel-selection/tile-size path change — for seq≈512 we probably hit a different tiling/path in our autotuner or cuBLAS changed heuristics. Could be kernel launch config or a cuBLAS algorithm selection change.
mike: Did you check KV cache behavior? Sometimes cache copy/evict patterns amplify matmul slowness when caching is warm vs cold.
alex: Yes — ran warm vs cold KV cache microbench: warm helps latency by ~10% but the matmul kernel delta remains. So KV caching isn't root cause, it's amplifying throughput loss under our batching heuristics. Batching combined with that particular kernel path seems to produce more SM divergence.
jamie: Can you share the exact driver/kernel version string from nvidia-smi + cuBLAS version? Also paste the autotuner decision log if available.
alex: nvidia-smi output:```
Driver Version: 535.54.03
CUDA Version: 12.3
cuBLAS: 12.3.1.2
Autotuner log (excerpt):
  seq<=256 -> tile=32x32 (matmul_32x32_fast)
  257<=seq<=1024 -> tile=16x64 (matmul_16x64_tiled)  <-- chosen for throughput
  seq>1024 -> tile=8x128 (matmul_8x128_long)
```
deploy-bot: Canary rollback available: tag release-2026-02-15. To rollback use `infra deploy --tag release-2026-02-15 --canary 5%`.
jamie: Short-term mitigation: add a driver-aware override in our kernel-selection table. If driver version >= 535.* and model arch == transformer_v1, prefer matmul_32x32_fast for seq in [256,1024] — we should auto-verify on startup by microbenchmarking the pair of candidates for the live hardware. Pseudocode:
```
for candidate in kernel_candidates:
  t = microbench(candidate, seq_samples=[128,512,1024])
choose candidate with best avg tokens/s across target seq distribution
cache choice per (arch, driver_version, sm_capability)
```
priya: Also add a quick rollback knob: `REDWOOD_FORCE_KERNEL=matmul_32x32_fast` and document it in infra runbooks. For rollout, canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% if microbench passes.
mike: Long-term fix: extend the autotuner to keep historical performance per driver build and automatically detect regressions after system upgrades. Add a daily regression job that runs weighted seq-distribution microbenchmarks (including KV-warm scenarios). Block fleet driver upgrades if regression > 7% on critical models.
alex: Good. Action items I propose: 1) short-term env var force and infra canary rollback (owner: priya). 2) Add startup microbench to kernel selector and driver-aware cache (owner: jamie). 3) Add nightly regression suite including KV-warm (owner: mike). 4) Communicate to SRE to pause mass driver rollout until we have autotune & tests.
priya: I can take 1) and help with runbook text. I'll add the env var, a simple check in the server init, and a fallback path if microbench times out. :+1:
jamie: I'll own 2). I'll add a lightweight microbench harness and persist kernel picks keyed by (gpu_arch, driver_version, cuBLAS_version). We should also log a confidence metric and expose an admin endpoint to override.
mike: I'll own 3). I'll extend the perf CI to run against a small model fleet matrix (seqs 128/512/2048, KV warm/cold, batch sizes 1/8/32) and fail PRs that touch runtime or infra that change these results beyond a threshold.
alex: Thanks all. I'll update incident channel and flag the canary rollback if perf doesn't improve within 2h. If anyone finds a quick patch to force different cuBLAS algo selection at the driver level, drop it here. :eyes:
